title: The Country of the Blind
focus: the arrogance and loneliness of seeing differently

teacherSummary.text: Mountaineer Nunez falls into an isolated Andean valley whose people have been blind for fifteen generations and no longer believe in sight. He expects 'In the Country of the Blind the One-eyed Man is King' but is treated as a madman. He falls in love with Medina-saroté; the elders agree to the marriage if his eyes, thought to be diseased, are removed. On the morning of the operation he climbs out of the valley and lies smiling under the stars.

My answer: He assumes his sight will make him a ruler, but the villagers have built a life without sight; the story shows that the proverb is arrogant and wrong.
